name: Poly Medicure Ltd
title: Poly Medicure Ltd - 531768 - Analyst Investor Meet Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA margin 28% on price hikes and inventory gain, with management guiding back to 25-27% and consolidated revenue guide of INR2,300-2,400 crore held; Middle East shipments stalled (-32%).

capex.quote: We expect to spend between INR200 crores to INR225 crores in the capex for FY27.

triggers.label: Gross margin 71.5% on price hikes
triggers.quote: Gross profit for Q1 was 71.5%, showing significant improvement due to better product mix and impact of price hikes implemented in Q1 and inventory gain.

triggers.label: Cash conversion cycle still 140 days
triggers.quote: In March, it was 140 days. Currently, it's also in a similar range of 140 days.

triggers.label: Middle East degrowth 32%
triggers.quote: The reason for low growth was 32% de-growth in the Middle East due to ongoing West Asia crisis.

triggers.label: Anti-dumping probe on China and Malaysia dialysers
triggers.quote: the government has initiated antidumping investigation into imports of dialyzers from China and Malaysia, and we have claimed for injury margin of 20%.

triggers.label: Renal degrowth 3.8%
triggers.quote: It degrew by 3.8% to INR43.2 crores.

guidance.quote: we are guiding for revenue of INR2,300 crores to INR2,400 crores, including the full year consolidation of PendraCare and Citieffe.
we maintained revenue guidance of INR1,900 crores to INR2,000 crores
Stand-alone EBITDA margin is expected to be between 25% to 27%.
The consolidated EBITDA margin expected to be in the range between 23% and 25%.
We expect to spend between INR200 crores to INR225 crores in the capex for FY27.
I expect that our gross margin should continue to reflect on historic margin trend of 68% to 69% in the near term.
we have set a goal to double our revenue by FY30
hopefully, year-end, we should end with a growth of around 15% to 18% in the business, maybe close to 20%

summary.headline: Poly Medicure Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 30.3% to INR525 crore (12.4% organic), with consolidated EBITDA margin at 24.1% and standalone at 28%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 30.3% to INR525 crore, of which INR72.3 crore came from acquisitions, leaving organic growth at 12.4% to INR453.1 crore. Standalone revenue rose 12.3% to INR431 crore and standalone EBITDA was INR120.8 crore (28% margin), above the 25-27% FY27 guidance, helped by price hikes and inventory gains. Middle East sales fell 32% due to West Asia logistics disruption, while renal degrew 3.8% amid Chinese pricing pressure. Management maintained FY27 guidance and launched a "PolyMed 3.0" target to double revenue by FY30.

financial_highlights.change: +12.3% YoY; domestic INR146 crore (+16.2%), international INR281.8 crore (+10%)
Flagged as above historic 68-69% trend; partly price hikes and inventory gain
From INR2.9 crore a year ago, led by PendraCare plus domestic scale-up

financial_highlights.value: Standalone working capital debt about INR250 crore (revolver); Citieffe loan about EUR 9 million, EUR 1.5-2 million repaid annually

segments.name: Infusion therapy
segments.commentary: Revenue INR259.2 crore, +11.1%, led by domestic growth of 20%+ from higher value-added products and price increases.

segments.name: Orthopedics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR49.2 crore, largely reflecting consolidation of Citieffe.

segments.name: Cardiology
segments.commentary: Revenue INR28.6 crore versus INR2.9 crore a year ago, driven by PendraCare acquisition and domestic scale-up.

segments.name: Renal
segments.commentary: Revenue INR43.2 crore, -3.8%; pressure from Chinese dialyzer imports, with company choosing price hikes over volume defence. Anti-dumping probe on China and Malaysia dialyzers initiated, 20% injury margin claimed.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Revenue INR141.9 crore, +18.5%, forming the balance of the consolidated mix.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated FY27 revenue guidance INR2,300-2,400 crore including full-year PendraCare and Citieffe; maintained after Q1.
Standalone FY27 revenue guidance INR1,900-2,000 crore; domestic expected to grow over 20%, international over 15%.
Standalone EBITDA margin guided at 25-27% for FY27, with management expecting to close near the upper end; standalone gross margin guided at 67-69% going forward.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 23-25%; consolidated gross margin expected at 71-72%.
FY27 capex INR200-225 crore; asset turns 1.2-1.4x.
Renal FY27 growth targeted at 15-18%, possibly close to 20%, contingent on anti-dumping outcome expected by year-end.
Long-term aspiration to double consolidated revenue by FY30 (PolyMed 3.0, 'Ascent'), roughly 80% organic and 20% inorganic; margins expected to be held at similar levels rather than expanded.
Faridabad (Palwal) plant expected online by March 2027, focused on orthopedics, transfusion and extra infusion capacity; Noida plant commercial from Q1 FY28, focused on cardiology.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at INR200-225 crore, with cash earmarked partly for two plants under construction.
Faridabad (Palwal) facility targeted online by March 2027 for orthopedics, transfusion and infusion capacity expansion.
Noida facility targeted for commercial operation in Q1 FY28, for cardiology expansion.
Asset turns of 1.2-1.4x expected to continue on the balance sheet.
PendraCare and Citieffe manufacturing shifts to India are in progress and at regulatory approval stage.
demand_pricing: Middle East: 32% decline due to West Asia crisis; orders are piling up at ports as ships are not calling and containers are hard to find. Management expects 20-25%+ growth once normalised.
Europe: +17.6% organic growth, back to the 17-18% planned rate after adding new customers; Southeast Asia also growing well.
US: exports expected at USD 3.5-4 million for FY27; current duty 10%.
Price hikes taken at start of FY27 to offset raw material increases; management sees raw material peak as past, with only minor further changes.
Renal faces pricing pressure from Chinese players importing duty-free via ASEAN FTA; company raised prices rather than defend volume.
PendraCare had about 20% Middle East exposure and is currently not growing; Citieffe growing in mid-to-high single digits.

qa_highlights.question: How will standalone revenue reach INR350-400 crore incremental growth, given about 12% growth in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is seasonally the lowest and early-year price hikes slowed sales, with recovery later in the quarter; momentum should lift Q2 onwards to meet guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What will the INR850 crore cash be used for?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic and inorganic expansion, including Brazil direct sales, technology in cardiology, oncology and orthopedics, adjacent technologies, and capex at two plants under construction.

qa_highlights.question: Will Middle East exports resume and will Q2 gross margin be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Shipping remains disrupted and orders are stuck at ports. Standalone gross margin is guided at 68-69%, so some correction from Q1's 71.5% is likely, with EBITDA broadly held by higher revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the 2x revenue goal and the implied gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated 2x is the target and standalone will grow faster than the subsidiaries; did not provide a precise breakdown.

qa_highlights.question: Gross debt and repayments?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone has only about INR250 crore working capital revolver; PendraCare has no long-term loan; Citieffe has about EUR 9 million loan with EUR 1.5-2 million repaid annually.

qa_highlights.question: Will the working capital cycle improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash conversion cycle remains around 140 days, same as March; management declined to give forward guidance given geopolitical delays.

risks_watch: Middle East shipments stalled by West Asia logistics disruption; Middle East orders piling up at ports, and recovery timing is not guided
Q1 standalone gross margin of 71.5% is above the 68-69% guided trend, so a Q2 margin correction is signalled by management
Renal faces Chinese dialyzer pricing pressure; anti-dumping outcome expected by year-end is the swing factor for the 15-18% renal growth target
PendraCare has about 20% Middle East exposure and is not growing; Citieffe growing mid-to-high single digits; inorganic growth contribution is unproven
Cash conversion cycle held at about 140 days with no forward guidance on improvement; export logistics costs up 2-3x in six months

Plant timelines: Faridabad (Palwal) online by March 2027 and Noida commercial from Q1 FY28, both dependent on regulatory approvals; PendraCare and Citieffe manufacturing shifts to India still awaiting approval
key_quotes: Customer demand in the region is intact, but given the current logistics and infrastructure bottlenecks, we are unable to meet that demand.
I expect that our gross margin should continue to reflect on historic margin trend of 68% to 69% in the near term.
So it's all about regulatory pathway, clinical studies.
So it's tough to give a forward-looking guidance on this at this point of time.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term 2x PolyMed 3.0 target and on maintaining FY27 guidance, but cautious and non-committal on specifics. Management declined to split employee and other expenses into fixed and variable, gave no precise breakdown of the 2x revenue gap, offered no forward cash conversion guidance, and said it would follow up separately on acquired-entity euro growth and margins.

adds.what: Faridabad (Palwal) plant, orthopedics, transfusion and extra infusion capacity
Noida plant, cardiology capacity, commercial operation

growth.why: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR2,300-2,400 crore (midpoint ~INR2,350 crore, ~21.5% above FY26 implied base is not stated directly; guidance held) is backed by two plants under construction (Faridabad by March 2027, Noida commercial Q1 FY28) and FY27 capex of INR200-225 crore, though Q1 organic growth was only 12.4% and Middle East fell 32%.
